'''World Industries''' is an American brand that offers skateboarding products, accessories and clothing. The company was founded by [[Steve Rocco]] in 1989. Later that year, Rocco was joined by skater, [[Rodney Mullen]], and then [[Mike Vallely]]. As of 2014, World Industries operates under GVS America, a subsidiary of INA Sports Inc. & FGL Sports Ltd.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Who We Are|url=https://gvsamerica.com/pages/who-we-are|access-date=2020-09-09|website=GVS America|language=en}}</ref> The company also makes and sells [[Longboard (skateboard)|longboards]].

The company was initially known for its cavalier attitude through its marketing and handling of their team riders, most notably through their use of [[Attack ad#Non-political usage|attack ads]] mocking rival skate companies as well as board designs that are either deemed offensive or bordering towards [[copyright infringement]], with which they simply brush off any [[cease-and-desist]] letters they receive from companies such as [[Disney]] and the [[Church of Scientology]] among others.<ref name="boardban">{{Cite web |date=2022-02-25 |title=10 Banned Board Graphics |url=https://doseskateboarding.com/articles/ten-banned-board-graphics |access-date=2024-10-06 |website=doseskateboarding.com}}</ref><ref name="wi">{{Cite web |title=Classic Ads: World Industries |url=https://www.boardworld.com.au/articles/classic-ads-world-industries |access-date=2024-10-06 |website=BOARDWORLD |language=en}}</ref>

==History==

===Blind===
In late-1989, [[Mark Gonzales]] approached Rocco with the desire to be involved in his own company. Gonzales was riding for [[Vision Street Wear|Vision]], which was one of the top 3 skateboard companies in the world at the time, alongside [[NHS, Inc.|Santa Cruz]] and [[Powell Peralta]]. Gonzales and Rocco decided to name the company [[Blind (company)|Blind]], in contrast to Gonzales' former sponsor. [[Jason Lee (actor)|Jason Lee]], who was, at the time, a World Industries team member, assisted with the development of the brand.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://shop.shredzshop.com/blogs/blog/blind-skateboards-heritage-re-issue-decks/?source=facebook|title=Behind the Boards: A look at the Blind Skateboards Heritage Re-Issue Decks|website=Shredz Shop|access-date=2019-03-30}}</ref>

===Plan B===
In 1991, wanting to break from H-Street, co-founder Mike Ternasky formed the company [[Plan B Skateboards|Plan B]] with an exclusive production and distribution alliance with World Industries. In the deal, Plan B marketed itself from [[San Diego]] while World Industries did the rest, paying a royalty fee to Plan B.{{Citation needed|date=July 2011}} Mike Ternasky was able to convince perennial freestyle world champion{{Citation needed|date=July 2011}} [[Rodney Mullen]] to switch to street skating thus becoming a member of the Plan B team.{{Citation needed|date=July 2011}}

In September 1993, Rick Howard defected with seven other riders from the fold of World Industries and started [[Girl Skateboards|Girl]]. Mike Ternasky was killed in a car accident in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-12-12 |title=Plan B honors Mike Ternasky posthumously |url=https://www.espn.com/action/skateboarding/story/_/id/8737171/the-original-plan-b-skateboards-team-honors-their-late-founder-mike-ternasky |access-date=2024-05-13 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> Plan B and World Industries parted ways in 1997, and was run by [[Danny Way]] and Colin McKay, closing its doors shortly thereafter in 1998. In March 2005, Plan B was resurrected by team member and part-owner, [[Danny Way]].

===Restructure and growth===
The years of 1996 to 1999 were years of significant restructuring and explosive growth for the company, led by the newly appointed executives, and subsequent shareholders, CEO Frank Messman and CFO Scott Drouillard.  By the end of 1998, World Industries and Blind had achieved the status of number one and number two brands in skateboard hardgoods.{{Citation needed|date=July 2011}}  This was in large part due to the re-positioning of the brands with [[Marc McKee]]'s hugely popular cartoon characters of Devil Man, Flame Boy and Wet Willy for World Industries, and the "Blind Reaper" for Blind.{{Citation needed|date=July 2011}}

===Kubic Marketing===
In October 1998, Steve Rocco and his then five other shareholder partners (including Rodney Mullen, Frank Messmann, and Scott Drouillard), sold a 70% majority interest of the company to an outside private equity group, SPC, while maintaining all key management and employees.{{Citation needed|date=July 2011}}  The company was valued at $29 million at the point of sale.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jenkemmag.com/home/2014/09/23/the-history-of-world-industries-and-its-29-million-dollar-sale/|title=The History of World INdustries and Its $29 Million Dollar Sale|publisher=Jenkem|first=Ian|last=Michna|date=September 23, 2014|access-date=February 27, 2018}}</ref>  A parent company emerged by the name of Kubic Marketing ("Kubic") which owned World Industries and [[Dwindle Distribution]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-jun-21-fi-43126-story.html|title=Free-Wheeling Skateboard Firm Trying to Roll Into Mainstream|work=Los Angeles Times|first=Denise|last=Gellene|date=June 21, 2000|access-date=February 27, 2018}}</ref>

In 1999, the parent company Kubic bought the then-largest retailer (catalog and internet) CCS in the skateboard industry for $21 million. In 2000, due to financial issues, the company sold CCS to Alloy, a publicly listed company for approximately $50 million.

===Globe International===
In 2002, [[Globe International]] Limited, an Australian public company, purchased all companies of Kubic, including World Industries.<ref>{{cite web|title=GLOBE BUYS KUBIC|url=http://business.transworld.net/4568/uncategorized/globe-buys-kubic/|work=Transworld Business|publisher=Bonnier Corporation|accessdate=9 September 2012|author=biz_editor|date=5 July 2002}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2002-jun-22-fi-globe22-story.html|title=Australian Firm to Buy Skateboard Company|work=Los Angeles Times|first=Leslie|last=Earnest|date=June 22, 2002|access-date=February 27, 2018}}</ref>

===i.e. Distribution===
On June 25, 2007, Globe International Limited sold the World Industries brand to i.e. Distribution.<ref name="Press">{{cite web|author=|first=|date=3 Sep 2020|title=Jenkem Buys World Industries|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jPfAy8Ajh5Q|accessdate=9 September 2012|publisher=Jenkem Magazine}}</ref>

As of February 2014, World Industries continues to sponsor a team of skateboarders; however, an official promotional flyer appeared on February 6, 2014, following the addition of a skateboard deck line to team rider Anthony Shetler's clothing brand "All I Need" (AIN). The flyer states: "Shetler and Timmy Knuth will have pro models," but as of February 20, 2014, both Shetler and Knuth remain on the World Industries website as team members, and no further information has been released.<ref>{{cite web|title=All I Need Premiere & Board Line|url=http://skateboarding.transworld.net/1000190754/news/need-premiere-board-line/|work=Transworld Skateboarding|publisher=Grind Media|accessdate=20 February 2014|author=TWS|date=6 February 2014}}</ref><ref name="Home">{{cite web|title=Home|url=http://www.worldindustries.com/|work=World Industries|accessdate=20 February 2014|date=20 February 2014}}</ref>

'''<big>Golden Viking Sports</big>'''

On August 10, 2014, World Industries was purchased by GVS America, a subsidiary that is wholly owned by INA Sports Inc. & FGL Sports Ltd.<ref>{{Cite web|title=World Industries Acquired By Golden Viking Sports {{!}} SGB Media Online|url=https://sgbonline.com/world-industries-acquired-by-golden-viking-sports/|access-date=2020-09-09|website=sgbonline.com|date=11 September 2014 }}</ref> Financial details of the purchase were not disclosed to the public.

==The Man Who Souled the World==
In 2007, [[Whyte House Entertainment|Whyte House Productions]] released ''The Man Who Souled the World'', a documentary about [[Steve Rocco]] and the creation of World Industries, as well as his other skateboard related companies and ventures.<ref>[https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0924461/ ''The Man Who Souled the World'' at IMDB]</ref> The film release was accompanied by a skateboard art exhibition (featuring Marc McKee's art) titled, "Censorship is Weak as F##k."
